title: Gold Miners Remain Resilient Despite Tighter Margins in Q2’26
gist: Metals Focus data show global average gold-mine AISC hit a record US$1,930/oz in Q2'26 (+22% y/y, 29th straight annual rise), driven by record sustaining capex (US$441/oz), diesel/labour inflation and site disruptions, while a 7.2% q/q gold price drop to US$4,512/oz cut AISC margins 16% to US$2,582/oz — still the second highest on record. Senior miners remain net-cash and kept paying out, but with gold at ~US$4,040/oz and AISC nearing US$2,000/oz, further margin contraction is expected through 2026 before a forecast 2027 gold price recovery widens margins.

insights.claim: Global average gold producer All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) rose 8% q/q and 22% y/y to a record US$1,930/oz in Q2 2026, per Metals Focus' Gold Mine Cost Service.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Cost floor for the gold mining industry is rising fast; margin models using older AISC assumptions overstate miner leverage to gold price.
insights.quote: Global average gold producer All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) rose by 8% q/q and 22% y/y to a record US$1,930/oz.

insights.claim: Q2 2026 marked the 29th consecutive year-on-year increase in global average gold mining AISC, showing cost inflation in gold mining is structural rather than cyclical.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite gold-miner cost deflation; persistent cost creep means miner equity upside depends on gold price outrunning costs.
insights.quote: This marked the 29th consecutive year-on-year increase, underlining the persistence of cost pressures.

insights.claim: Sustaining capex replaced royalties as the main driver of higher gold mining AISC in Q2 2026, rising 34% q/q and 25% y/y to a record US$441/oz and accounting for roughly 80% of the US$139/oz q/q net AISC increase.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Cost driver has shifted from price-linked royalties (which fall with gold) to capex that stays sticky even if gold prices drop.
insights.quote: Sustaining capex replaced royalties as the principal driver of higher AISC in Q2’26

insights.claim: Sustaining capital's share of the gold mining industry cost base rose to 23% in Q2 2026 from 18% in Q1 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A rising capex share of AISC signals reinvestment needs that compete with shareholder returns.

insights.claim: The Q2 2026 rise in gold miners' sustaining capex was concentrated in a minority of operations, and deferred spending timing amplified quarterly unit costs without necessarily implying a comparable rise in annual expenditure.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Read single-quarter AISC spikes cautiously; check annual guidance before extrapolating capex-driven cost jumps.
insights.quote: deferred spending raised unit costs without necessarily implying a comparable increase in annual expenditure

insights.claim: Agnico Eagle's sustaining expenditure rose 21% q/q to US$237m in Q2 2026, with most of the increase at Detour Lake and Fosterville.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Watch whether Agnico Eagle's Detour Lake/Fosterville capex normalises in H2 or signals a higher run-rate.

insights.claim: B2Gold's Goose mine in Canada posted AISC of US$6,390/oz in Q2 2026 as catch-up spending deferred from Q1 coincided with a crushing-circuit fire that restricted throughput and cut gold sales.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Goose ramp-up remains a key execution risk for B2Gold; one-off disruptions can blow out single-asset unit costs.
insights.quote: Restricted throughput and lower-than-expected gold sales compounded higher sustaining expenditure, taking AISC to US$6,390/oz.

insights.claim: Newmont incurred additional costs during downtime at its Cadia mine in Australia after an April 2026 seismic event, with lower gold and by-product sales and weaker by-product credits raising reported costs; the mine returned to normal in mid-June, marking it as a temporary rather than persistent cost hit.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Strip Cadia's Q2 disruption out when assessing Newmont's underlying cost trend.
insights.quote: The mine returned to normal operations in mid-June, distinguishing temporary setbacks from persistent cost inflation.

insights.claim: Production at operations covered by Metals Focus' Gold Mine Cost Service recovered 1.6% q/q in Q2 2026 with grades up 1.4%, but output and grades were down 4.4% and 3.1% y/y, so costs rose despite a modest quarterly output recovery.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Falling y/y grades and output mean fixed costs spread over fewer ounces, structurally lifting unit costs and constraining mine supply.
insights.locator: Despite this disruption, production at the operations

insights.claim: Gold miners' Cash Operating Costs rose 6% q/q and 18% y/y to US$1,215/oz in Q2 2026, while Total Cash Costs rose 4% q/q and 22% y/y to US$1,406/oz.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Onsite cost inflation is broad, not just capex timing; it will persist into H2 margins.

insights.claim: Labour and diesel were key gold-mining cost pressures in Q2 2026, with Agnico Eagle and AngloGold Ashanti citing higher labour and diesel costs y/y and Newmont reporting higher diesel prices.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold miners carry embedded short-oil exposure; rising diesel prices are a direct margin headwind.

insights.claim: Fuel contracts and hedges only delay gold miners' energy cost exposure: replenishment at higher prices prolongs cost pressure, as when Agnico Eagle bought about 70% of its Nunavut diesel needs through the 2027 delivery season at prices roughly 30% above its 2026 budget, net of hedges.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Locks in higher 2027 energy costs for Agnico Eagle's Nunavut operations; expect cost guidance pressure next year.
insights.quote: Fuel contracts and hedges can limit immediate exposure, but replenishment at higher prices may prolong cost pressure.

insights.claim: Westgold Resources' long-term procurement agreements prevented supply interruptions but not price exposure, with higher diesel prices adding A$12m to its June-quarter 2026 costs.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Procurement contracts protect volume, not price; smaller producers' margins are exposed to fuel spikes.

insights.claim: Supply-chain constraints in Q2 2026 hit not only the cost but the availability of mining inputs: Resolute Mining reported logistics difficulties, higher fuel and reagent costs and explosives supply problems at Syama in Mali, and Evolution Mining's Mungari in Australia suffered about three days of grid-power outages.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Input availability risk can cut production as well as raise costs; monitor procurement and power reliability, especially in West Africa.
insights.quote: Supply-chain constraints in Q2’26 not only affected the cost, but also the availability of essential inputs.

insights.claim: Lower gold prices cut average royalty and production-tax costs 11% q/q to US$185/oz in Q2 2026, though they were still 53% higher y/y; their share of AISC eased to 9.6% from 11.6% in Q1.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Royalties act as a partial automatic stabiliser on miner margins when gold falls, but only partly offset other cost inflation.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, lower gold prices provided partial support

insights.claim: Lower gold prices do not reverse fiscal changes: Newmont booked a full quarter of Ghana's increased royalties in Q2 2026, making royalty relief uneven across producers.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Resource-nationalism-driven royalty hikes (e.g. Ghana) are a one-way ratchet that permanently lifts cost bases for exposed miners.
insights.quote: lower prices do not reverse fiscal changes

insights.claim: Gold miners' corporate general and administrative costs fell 21% q/q to US$82/oz in Q2 2026, softening but not offsetting higher operating expenses and sustaining capex.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: G&A savings are too small to move AISC materially.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, lower gold prices provided partial support

insights.claim: The average gold price fell 7.2% q/q to US$4,512/oz in Q2 2026, and combined with higher costs, average AISC margins contracted 16% q/q to US$2,582/oz.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Miner margins are operationally levered both ways: a 7% gold price drop produced a 16% margin drop.
insights.locator: Margins Retreat but Cash Generation Remains Strong

insights.claim: Despite the Q2 2026 squeeze, gold prices were still 37% higher y/y, AISC margins were up 52% y/y, and the average margin was the second highest in Metals Focus' dataset.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Margin compression is from exceptional levels; miners retain a large cushion, so sell-offs on q/q squeezes may overshoot.
insights.quote: The average margin was still the second highest in our dataset, leaving miners with a substantial cushion despite the quarterly squeeze.
insights.locator: Margins Retreat but Cash Generation Remains Strong

themes.theme: Cash flow, buybacks and net cash balance sheets

insights.claim: AngloGold Ashanti generated US$727m of free cash flow in Q2 2026, up 36% y/y, and Kinross generated attributable FCF of US$727m, up 12% y/y.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Large producers are still producing strong FCF despite margin compression.
insights.locator: Margins Retreat but Cash Generation Remains Strong

insights.claim: Endeavour Mining's free cash flow fell to US$149m in Q2 2026 from US$613m in Q1 due to higher tax payments, lower realised gold prices, higher operating costs and greater investing outflows, yet it still paid about US$200m in dividends and repurchased US$42m of shares.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Endeavour's distributions exceeded quarterly FCF; sustainability depends on balance sheet and gold price recovery.
insights.locator: Margins Retreat but Cash Generation Remains Strong

insights.claim: OceanaGold's free cash flow fell to US$130m in Q2 2026 from US$255m in Q1, but it returned US$78m to shareholders, including US$58m via buybacks.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Mid-tier producers are maintaining buybacks through softer quarters.
insights.locator: Shareholder distributions continued despite lower quarterly

insights.claim: Gold miners' shareholder distributions in Q2 2026 were funded by financial resources accumulated during the gold price upswing, not just current-quarter cash flow, letting payouts continue as quarterly FCF fell.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Payout durability is a balance-sheet question; screen miners on net cash rather than single-quarter FCF.
insights.quote: These distributions demonstrate the role of accumulated financial resources, rather than current-quarter cash flow alone, in supporting shareholder returns.
insights.locator: Shareholder distributions continued despite lower quarterly

insights.claim: AngloGold Ashanti repurchased about US$666m principal of outstanding bonds in April 2026, lowering gross debt and interest obligations, and ended June with US$991m of net cash.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Deleveraging lowers AngloGold's risk profile and frees future cash for distributions.
insights.locator: Cash was also used to reduce

insights.claim: Newmont, Agnico Eagle and Kinross ended June 2026 with reported net cash of US$3.4bn, US$3.3bn and US$1.9bn respectively, giving flexibility to sustain investment and distributions through weaker prices or disruption.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Senior gold miners are net-cash; downturn risk to dividends/buybacks is low near term.
insights.locator: Cash was also used to reduce

insights.claim: Global gold mining AISC is approaching US$2,000/oz, and expensive fuel purchases plus continuing supply-chain and inflationary pressures are expected to keep costs rising.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Model AISC crossing US$2,000/oz; miner earnings estimates need higher cost assumptions.
insights.quote: As AISC approaches US$2,000/oz, expensive fuel purchases, continuing supply-chain and inflationary pressures are expected to sustain cost increases.

insights.claim: The gold price averaged US$4,266/oz in Q3 2026, down 5.5% q/q, and was around US$4,040/oz at the time of writing in November 2026, setting up further gold-miner margin contraction for the rest of 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Expect weaker Q3/Q4 miner earnings and margins; near-term gold equity catalysts are negative.
insights.quote: this sets the stage for further margin contraction over the remainder of 2026

insights.claim: A forecast gold price recovery in 2027 would raise royalty costs but more than offset them through higher revenues, widening gold-miner margins and strengthening balance sheets.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Positions gold miners as a 2027 recovery trade if the gold price rebound materialises.
insights.quote: a forecast recovery in gold prices would lift royalty costs but this should be more than offset through higher revenues

insights.claim: Q2 2026 represented a retreat from exceptional gold-miner margins rather than a collapse in cash generation, with gold prices still historically high and balance sheets robust.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Frames the cost squeeze as a normalisation, not a solvency or payout threat.
insights.quote: Q2’26 marked a retreat from exceptional margins rather than a collapse in cash generation.
